title: Docs-site emergency patch and rollback playbook
author: Maya Patel
summary: Operational runbook for on-call and docs engineering to triage, patch, and if necessary roll back critical regressions in the Docs site (content, snippets, and hosted SDK examples). Focus is on minimizing customer impact and ensuring reproducibility of fixes.
intended_audience: Docs engineers, developer-experience oncall, platform SRE, release manager, developer advocates
prerequisites: Access: docs-site deploy pipeline, CMS admin, GitHub repo write for docs-source, staging environment. Required tools: deploy-cli (v1.4+), curl, jq, playground-sandbox, slack and PagerDuty access. A validated staging snapshot (tagged) must be available before any emergency action.
emergency_triggers: 1) Production site content severability: missing API keys in published snippets, live examples returning malformed JSON. 2) CSE/SDK canonical sample regressions causing runtime errors for customers. 3) PII or security-sensitive content accidentally published. 4) Critical visual or navigation breaks that block sign-ups or SDK onboarding flows.
roles_and_oncall:
- Primary: Docs Oncall (first responder)
- Secondary: DevX Engineer (patch author)
- SRE: Infrastructure and deploy rollback
- Release Manager: stakeholder comms and approval for customer-notice
- Legal/Security (if PII/exposure)
Each incident must set a Slack channel #docs-incident-<YYYYMMDD>-<initials> and assign a PagerDuty incident with severity (sev1 if site unavailable/signups blocked; otherwise sev2).
initial_triage_checklist:
1) Confirm the scope: is the issue content-only (HTML/CSS/MD) or a runtime/example failure (JS, hosted sandbox, serverless functions)?
2) Capture reproducible steps and affected URLs.
3) Take a production snapshot: curl -sS <url> > /tmp/prod-snapshot-<ts>.html and upload to incident channel.
4) Check recent deploys: deploy-cli history --limit 20 | grep docs-site.
5) Identify the earliest bad deploy tag or commit SHA.
hotfix_patch_steps:
A. For content-only regressions (no backend changes):
  1. Create a fork/branch in docs-source repo: git checkout -b hotfix/docs-<short-desc>-<ts>.
  2. Revert the offending commit or apply minimal content change.
  3. Run local build and smoke tests: npm run docs:build && npm run docs:smoke.
  4. Open a pull request titled: [HOTFIX] <short-desc> and assign Docs Oncall + DevX.
  5. If change is trivial (typo, snippet fix) and reviewers are available, merge with fast-track label and CI exemptions as allowed by policy.
  6. Deploy to staging: deploy-cli deploy --env staging --tag hotfix/docs-<ts>.
  7. Validate staging via checklist below.
  8. Promote to prod during a low-traffic window (unless severity mandates immediate deploy): deploy-cli promote --from staging --to prod --tag hotfix/docs-<ts>.
B. For runtime/example failures (requires code changes):
  1. Branch in repo containing the SDK snippet runtime or hosted example service.
  2. Run unit tests and example harnesses.
  3. If fix requires backend change, coordinate with SRE for canary: deploy-cli canary --service examples-host --percent 5 --tag hotfix/examples-<ts>.
  4. Monitor metrics (errors, latency) for 15 minutes; if green, widen to 25%, then 100%.
step_by_step_rollback:
1) If the root cause is a recent deploy and a hotfix is not feasible quickly, perform a rollback: deploy-cli rollback --service docs-site --to-tag <previous-stable-tag> --reason "Emergency rollback: <short-reason>".
2) SRE must coordinate a rolling restart and verify CDN invalidation is not required.
3) Post-rollback validation: run the validation_checks below and confirm via incident channel.
4) Do not delete the bad tag/commit; create a follow-up PR to fix root cause.
5) If rollback involves DB migrations or schema changes, escalate to Database team and follow the DB rollback playbook (link in related_pages).
validation_checks:
- Smoke: home page and top 10 landing pages return 200 within 1.5s.
- Snippets: all canonical SDK snippets execute in the 'playground-sandbox' with success == true. Use: curl -sS -X POST https://playground.internal/run -d '{"snippet_id":"<id>"}' | jq .status
- Auth flows: sign-up flow must complete end-to-end in staging sandbox.
- Visual: run a quick Percy/visual snapshot for the impacted pages.
- Search/index: verify the search index updated if content changed (search-admin status).
communication_templates:
Slack incident open (quick):
[SEV{level}] Docs site incident: <short-desc>
Scope: pages affected, example ids.
Status: triage in progress.
Owner: @<primary>.
Next update: +15m.
Email/Customer Notice (if PII or broad impact): use predefined template in /confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/customer-communication-templates (include rollback or hotfix ETA).
examples_and_cli_commands:
- Find recent docs deploys:
  deploy-cli history --service docs-site --limit 10
- Promote a staging tag to prod:
  deploy-cli promote --service docs-site --from staging --to prod --tag <tag>
- Rollback to previous stable tag:
  deploy-cli rollback --service docs-site --to-tag <stable-tag> --comment "Emergency rollback"
- Run snippet harness locally (example snippet id 42):
  curl -sS -X POST https://playground.internal/run -d '{"snippet_id":"42","env":"staging"}' | jq .
- Quick local build and serve:
  git checkout <branch> && npm ci && npm run docs:build && npm run docs:serve -- --port 8080
postmortem_and_followup:
- Create an incident ticket in Jira: DOCS-INC-<YYYY>-<NNN>.
- Required artifacts: prod snapshot, staging snapshot, failing commit SHAs, deploy history, timeline of actions.
- Responsible: Primary writes the first draft within 48 hours; reviewers: DevX and SRE.
- Outcome: classify as 'process', 'code', or 'third-party' and add corrective actions with owners and due dates.
- For any customer-facing incidents, prepare a public postmortem version (redacted) within 7 days.
known_risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: Fast-track merges can bypass full integration tests. Mitigation: allow only docs-only trivial changes; require at least one reviewer and an automated smoke run.
- Risk: CDN caching hides rollbacks. Mitigation: include CDN purge step in rollback template and verify TTLs.
- Risk: Hotfix introduces regressions. Mitigation: use canary and automated snippet harness with fail-fast thresholds.
appendix_snippet_examples:
1) Example: Reproducing a broken SDK snippet (Node):
```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://playground.internal/run -d '{"snippet_id":"42","runtime":"node16"}' | jq .
```
2) Minimal patch PR title and checklist:
[HOTFIX] docs: fix broken sdk sample in quickstart
- [ ] Reproduce locally
- [ ] Add unit/regression test for snippet harness
- [ ] CI smoke green
- [ ] Staging validated
- [ ] Prod promoted
